positive_findings: Exact production VCS recompilation reproduces all 128 requests, 2,048 word checks, 120 II1 checks, directed stalls/attacks and seven nonzero SVA covers.
An independent 65,538-request VCS campaign naturally crosses 16-bit token wrap with 65,537 consecutive II1 intervals and no loss, duplication or identity mismatch.
Full payload plus start/last/width/tag/token remains stable through skid stall, and same-cycle skid pop plus new request immediately recovers to fallthrough II1.
Independent M136/M137 VCS A/B measures delivery at 2/1 cycles while both sustain II1; the bridge-local latency reduction is real under the frozen behavioral macro contract.
Both DC evidence manifests verify. The A/B uses the same 1,303-port interface, tool, libraries, SDC, Tcl, 3 ns clock, ideal clock, ZeroWireload and zero macros.
Independent arithmetic confirms 22.4492748926% area, 10.0613824393% cell and 46.9471947195% sequential-cell reductions; the sequential counts reconcile exactly to the removed storage structure.
Read-only mapped-DDC reports show positive slack for all named fallthrough/control paths under the existing port-cut constraints.

findings.title: Reset restarts the token epoch without flushing outstanding macro responses
findings.observation: The interface has no macro reset/flush acknowledgement or response epoch. An independent attack accepts pre-reset token 0, resets before its response, accepts post-reset token 0, then returns the stale pre-reset token-0 payload. M137 reports no protocol error and accepts the stale payload under the new request's metadata.
findings.impact: A delayed response across reset can silently corrupt data rather than fail closed. Four production reset recoveries occur only after completed fault attacks and do not cover reset with an outstanding macro request. Natural wrap is safe under strict one-cycle operation, but reset immediately reuses token zero and bypasses that protection.
findings.required_fix: Define reset ownership at the macro boundary. Preferred repair: add macro_flush_req/flush_ack, block request_ready after reset until all pre-reset responses are invalidated, and include a generation/epoch in the wrapper identity that cannot alias across reset. Alternatively freeze and assert an atomic top-level reset contract that guarantees the macro wrapper destroys every outstanding response before bridge release. Add the exact stale-response replay attack and reset-at-every-pipeline-phase covers.

findings.title: The fixed-one-cycle token-echo macro remains a behavioral wrapper contract
findings.observation: Foundry SRAM macros, a wrapper that generates/echoes tokens, macro reset behavior, and per-bank response valid/skew are absent. Wrong/missing/unsolicited aggregate responses are detected only after an external wrapper has already assembled all sixteen banks.
findings.impact: Functional bridge evidence is strong, but macro correctness, partial-bank failure and native timing are not established.
findings.minimal_fix: Implement the smallest 16-bank macro wrapper with request identity, per-bank return-valid collection, skew timeout, reset/flush protocol and aggregate response token; drive M137 through it before macro-inclusive claims.

findings.title: Two-to-one delivery is bridge latency, not throughput or system acceleration
findings.observation: Matched VCS measures first delivery at two cycles for M136 and one for M137, a 50% reduction or isolated 2.0x bridge-latency ratio. Both designs sustain II1, so steady-state throughput gain is exactly absent in the admitted ready trace.
findings.impact: The result must not be described as a 2x accelerator, full-module speedup or system speedup. Its end-to-end benefit depends on how often an unpipelined first-response latency lies on the workload critical path.
findings.minimal_fix: Report bridge latency and throughput as separate metrics. Insert the measured one-cycle delta into the ordered module trace and use an Amdahl/critical-path composition; retain throughput_gain=false unless integrated stalls change.

findings.title: Fallthrough introduces explicit macro/consumer/upstream combinational paths
findings.observation: Mapped-DDC audits show macro words to response words, macro valid to response valid, response ready to request ready, and macro token to request ready paths. They meet the current port-cut constraints with 1.9747, 1.9074, 2.1465 and 1.7924 ns slack respectively, but the flow assumes 0.25 ns input arrival, ideal clock and ZeroWireload.
findings.impact: The standalone logic is healthy, yet actual macro access, bank wiring and external ready/valid logic can consume the margin or create a top-level combinational loop.
findings.minimal_fix: Run macro-aware PT/topographical timing using real macro clk-to-Q and placed wiring; perform a top-level ready/valid loop audit. Add a registered-mode fallback if the direct control/data budget fails.

findings.title: Production assertions do not fully encode the reviewed boundaries
findings.observation: The stalled-response stability property covers words, tag and token but omits start, last and width. There is no assertion for exact accept equality, token increment/wrap, same-cycle skid-pop plus new-request conservation, or in-flight reset epoch safety. Independent directed tests pass the first four functional behaviors and expose the reset defect.
findings.impact: Future edits can regress metadata or wrap/pop behavior without violating the current property set.
findings.minimal_fix: Extend stall stability to all response fields; assert accept equivalences, token successor including ffff-to-0000, exact skid pop/store conservation and the repaired reset/flush epoch rule. Add formal or constrained-random reachability around simultaneous edges.

findings.title: Logic-only area savings are real but not macro-inclusive PPA or energy
findings.observation: M137 removes 1,368.990009 um2 and 754 cells at the standard-cell port cut, dominated by 569 fewer sequential cells. Both A/B runs contain zero SRAM macros, zero interconnect area, no propagated clock, no SAIF/PTPX and no RTL-to-netlist Formality seal.
findings.impact: The 22.449275% area and 46.947195% sequential-cell reductions are citable only for bridge standard-cell logic. They do not imply the same total accelerator area or energy percentage.
findings.minimal_fix: Add Formality, identical macro instances and placed wiring to both A/B variants, then run SAIF/PTPX on the same traffic/stall traces and report absolute plus percentage total-area/power/energy changes.

ordered_actions: Close the reset-epoch stale-response alias with macro flush/ack or an explicit atomic reset contract plus generation identity.
Implement the minimal 16-bank wrapper with token, per-bank valid/skew and reset behavior.
Extend SVA for full metadata stability, token wrap, pop+new conservation and reset phases.
Run Formality and macro-aware physical timing on all new fallthrough paths.
Preserve delivery 2-to-1 and II1 as separate bridge metrics; compose workload/system benefit only from ordered traces.
Run matched macro-inclusive area and SAIF/PTPX before making total PPA or energy claims.
claim_boundary: M137 admits exact-SHA fixed-latency bridge functionality and a fair standard-cell logic-only DC A/B. It has a reset-epoch P1 and does not admit macro-inclusive PPA, power, throughput gain, physical speedup, system speedup, DATE headline or best-paper readiness.
